instructions:
You are labelling memory write decisions for an engineering-memory system. Each row is one candidate memory that a system extracted from a public open-source project discussion (a GitHub issue or pull-request thread; contributor names are pseudonyms such as contributor-1a2b3c4d). The row shows `transcript_excerpt` (turns as "[speaker] text", which may not cover the whole thread), `item` (the candidate memory: a preference, convention or stance, rendered as "<category> preference (<polarity>, strength s): <key> about <entity>") and `quote` (the text the system cited as its evidence).

Decide `label`: should the memory system STORE this item as a durable memory about this project or its contributors, or SKIP it?

store when all of these hold: (1) the quote, read in the excerpt, states or directly implies the item (right subject, right polarity); (2) the item says something durable and specific: a project convention, design decision, technical preference, constraint or recurring practice that would help someone working on this project later; (3) it is attributed sensibly (a preference of a participant or of the project, not a misreading).

skip when any of these hold: the quote does not support the item or contradicts it; the item is generic filler that would be true of almost any collaboration (for example polite communication, being open to feedback, doing code review in general) with no project-specific content; it is a one-off transient remark (a single request in passing, a status update, a thank-you) with no lasting value; it is too vague to act on; or it misattributes or overstates what was said.

The strength number in the item is not part of the judgement. Judge only from the row.
